label: Transverse freedom
title: Finite width can be packed; Rule32 correction depth adds no independent transverse capacity through depth four
kind: Exact capacity theorem and bounded diagnostic
summary: Any fixed finite strip width can be column-packed into a 1D product alphabet, while an unbounded full strip defeats every fixed target alphabet and longitudinal expansion budget. On the inherited Rule32 family, correction tuples add no new whole-field distinctions beyond depth zero through h=4 on rings 6–12.
takeaway: Nominal transverse width is not enough: a candidate spatial axis needs a resource that cannot simply be packed into fixed one-dimensional state. The Rule32 correction stack remains source-bounded under this test.
